title: Embedding backpressure & capacity audit for tenant-aware throughput
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Recent customer reports and load tests show tail latency spikes and fair-share violations for embeddings when mix of small (1-10 token) and large (100-1000 token) requests hit the same pool. Our current autoscaler reacts to average GPU utilization and queue depth, which leads to either overprovisioning or long tail queues causing rate limit bursts and customer impact.

Goal: Design and implement a tenant-aware backpressure and capacity audit that improves end-to-end P95 latency under realistic mixed workloads, preserves SLAs for high-priority tenants, and reduces unnecessary scale-ups during transient bursts. Deliver a runbook, a conservative rollout plan, and a set of dashboards/alerts.

Scope: This ticket covers design, prototype, and capacity planning artifacts for the backpressure system and an accompanying audit of current queueing behaviour. Implementations will touch serving runtime (queueing & admission), routing policy (priority tagging), autoscaler config, and monitoring dashboards. Actual autoscaler code changes will be in follow-up tickets.

Constraints and non-goals: We will not change model execution kernels or quantization as part of this ticket. Full on-prem private deployment integration will be documented but implemented in separate work.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Add tenant-priority and request-cost estimates at admission time. Request-cost is a simple token-cost heuristic computed from sequence length and embedding dimension.
2) Implement soft backpressure: if per-tenant queue length or estimated cost queues exceed thresholds, mark lower-priority requests with a short retry-after hint and move them to a throttled queue while allowing high-priority requests through.
3) Extend autoscaler inputs: include predicted steady-state token/sec, weighted queue length, and a 60s burst score to avoid oscillation on transient bursts.
4) Capacity audit: run 4 representative load profiles (small-only, large-only, mixed-even, mixed-spiky) and capture scale events, time-to-scale, rejected requests, and cost delta.
5) Produce runbook and dashboards with SLOs and alert thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by runtime and infra leads
Backpressure prototype integrated into staging serving with configurable flags
Capacity audit completed for 4 load profiles and results uploaded
Dashboards capture per-tenant queueing and burst score
Canary rollout plan with rollback criteria documented
notes: 2026-03-03: Spike in p95 observed for tenant T-Alpha during mixed workload replay. Reproduced locally with synthetic mix.
2026-03-05: Chose token-cost heuristic v1: estimated_cost = max(1, ceil(seq_len / 32)) * (embedding_dim / 512). Needs verification vs real tokenization.
2026-03-07: Trade-off discussion with Product: conservative retries reduce perceived error but increase client complexity; decided to return 429 with Retry-After for best UX and metrics.
2026-03-09: Infra requested autoscaler metric window increase from 30s -> 60s to reduce flapping during transient bursts.

2026-03-11: Design doc reviewed by Anika Patel (SRE) and Ben Ford (Runtime). Ben flagged potential GPU utilization starvation in rare low-latency pools; mitigation added: per-pool emergency drain for throttled queue.
rollout_plan: feature gated by runtime flag: embeddings.backpressure.enabled=false by default
deploy prototype to staging pool 'emb-staging-a' behind flag
run capacity audit load profiles against staging and collect metrics (3 runs per profile)
enable gate for 5% of production traffic (canary) with elevated logging for those requests
monitor for 2 hours, validate no increase in user-visible 5xx errors and p95 improved by target
if stable, ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 24h observation windows
test_plan: synthetic load harness using k6 + recorded request traces from production
profile small-only: 10k qps of ~8-token requests for 30m
profile large-only: 1k qps of ~512-token requests for 30m
mixed-spiky: baseline 1k qps with 30s spikes to 8k qps every 10m
validate metrics: time-to-scale, queue length, success rate, customer-impact tags

compute and expose 60s burst score as gauge
